CORRECTION AFTER QC FAILURE (attempt 1 rejected — obey over any conflicting earlier line): attempt 1 produced an ordinary point collar. The words "hexagon", "faceted" and "six-sided" did not carry the geometry, so here is the outline as an explicit path. Trace EACH collar leaf from the band outward as follows: (1) leave the collar band at the neck and run outward and slightly down to an OUTER CORNER sitting near the widest part of the collar; (2) from that corner the edge TURNS BACK INWARD and runs in a near-straight line toward the centre front, rising slightly, to a shallow INWARD NOTCH — a distinct concave step, not a curve; (3) from that notch the edge turns again and runs down and inward to the LONG DEEP CENTRE-FRONT POINT. So the outer edge of each leaf CHANGES DIRECTION AT LEAST TWICE between the band and the tip, giving each leaf a stepped profile, and the two leaves read together as a six-sided silhouette. FAILURE CONDITION, STATED EXPLICITLY: a leaf whose outer edge runs in ONE straight line from the band to the tip is WRONG and is a rejection. There must be a visible corner and a visible notch on each leaf, crisply pressed and clearly readable, symmetric left to right.
